properties.title: NX-100 Wall-Mounted Installation Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the standard procedure for mechanically and electrically installing a Nova AC 100 (NX-100) 7.4 kW single-socket wall-mounted charger at a small business or employee parking site.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the installation site has a suitable wall structure rated to support the charger's weight and vibration load. Confirm an available single-phase circuit sized per the site electrical survey and local code. Confirm the customer has scheduled a qualified electrician or NMG-certified technician for the final connection. Review the site electrical survey and single-line diagram. Confirm Wi-Fi signal strength or Ethernet drop availability at the mounting location.
properties.requiredTools: Drill and wall anchors appropriate to the wall substrate, torque screwdriver, cable stripping and crimping tools, multimeter, insulation resistance (megohmmeter) tester, RCD/GFCI test instrument, spirit level, NMG installation bracket kit, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves connection to mains electrical supply. Installation and final connection must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or an NMG-certified installation technician, in compliance with local electrical codes. Obtain all required electrical work permits before starting. Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) on the upstream distribution board before opening any enclosure. Wear appropriate PPE (insulated gloves, safety glasses, arc-rated clothing where applicable). Do not proceed with commissioning until post-installation continuity, insulation resistance, and RCD/GFCI trip testing have been completed and recorded.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Confirm isolation of the target circuit at the distribution board and apply lockout/tagout. 2. Mount the wall bracket at the height specified in the NX-100 installation guide, using anchors rated for the unit's weight. 3. Route and terminate the supply cable into the charger's connection compartment following the wiring diagram in the TechSpec sheet; do not deviate from the specified conductor sizing. 4. Secure the charger body onto the bracket and confirm mechanical stability. 5. Connect Ethernet cable or configure Wi-Fi credentials per the Ethernet/Wi-Fi configuration procedure. 6. Restore power at the distribution board only once the electrician confirms all terminations are correctly torqued and covers are secured. 7. Power on the unit and confirm the front-panel status LED reaches a steady 'ready' state.
properties.validation: Perform and record continuity, insulation resistance, and RCD/GFCI trip tests per local code before energizing. Confirm the unit registers with the Polaris backend and reports status 'Available'. Perform a test charge session using a test vehicle or load simulator and confirm correct energy metering in Polaris. Confirm the unit responds correctly to a remote start/stop command from Polaris.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If the unit fails to power on, verify upstream breaker position and supply voltage at the terminal block. If the unit powers on but does not appear in Polaris, verify the network connection per the Ethernet Configuration procedure and confirm the unit's registration credentials. If RCD/GFCI testing fails, do not energize the circuit; escalate to the electrician of record.
properties.escalation: If electrical test failures persist after two attempts, or if a client-specific electrical anomaly is found, escalate to the NMG Field Engineering team via the installer portal, referencing the site survey ID.
properties.tags: installation, NX-100, wall-mount, single-phase, AC charger

properties.title: Annual Charger Inspection Procedure (All Products)
properties.purpose: Describes the standard annual inspection procedure applicable to all NMG charging products (NX-100 through DX-360), covering mechanical, electrical, and functional checks to confirm continued safe and reliable operation.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the unit's service history and any open known issues or fault codes in Polaris before the site visit. Confirm the correct annual inspection checklist variant for the product model (AC vs. DC-specific items differ).
properties.requiredTools: Multimeter, insulation resistance tester, RCD/GFCI test instrument, torque wrench, visual inspection checklist, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure includes opening the unit's electrical compartment for torque and connection checks. This work must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician. Apply lockout/tagout before opening any electrical enclosure. Do not re-energize until all checks are complete and enclosures are secured.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Review Polaris fault history and open known issues for the unit prior to arrival. 2. Perform a visual inspection of the enclosure, cabling, connectors, and mounting/foundation for damage, corrosion, or looseness. 3. Isolate and lockout/tagout the supply, open the electrical compartment, and re-torque terminations to specification, checking for signs of overheating or arcing. 4. Perform insulation resistance and RCD/GFCI trip testing and record results. 5. Restore power and confirm the unit reaches a steady 'ready' state and reports correctly to Polaris. 6. Perform a test charge session and confirm correct metering and, where applicable, RFID/OCPP functionality. 7. Log the completed inspection and any findings in Polaris.
properties.validation: Confirm all recorded test values (insulation resistance, RCD trip time) are within the product's specified tolerances. Confirm no new fault codes are logged during or immediately after the test charge session. Confirm the inspection record is filed in Polaris with a pass/fail outcome.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If insulation resistance has degraded but remains within tolerance, note the trend for comparison at the next annual inspection rather than treating it as an immediate fault. If a termination shows signs of overheating, do not simply re-torque and close up — investigate root cause (e.g. undersized conductor, loose factory termination) before returning the unit to service.
properties.escalation: Escalate any failed electrical test or evidence of overheating/arcing to NMG Field Engineering before returning the unit to service.
properties.tags: annual inspection, preventive maintenance, all products, electrical testing

properties.title: NX-200 Pedestal Installation Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the standard procedure for installing a freestanding Nova AC 200 (NX-200) 22 kW pedestal charger for corporate parking or hospitality sites, including foundation, mechanical mounting, and electrical connection.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm a completed civil works foundation (concrete pad or approved footing) meeting the NX-200 foundation drawing tolerances and cure time. Confirm availability of a single-phase or three-phase circuit as specified by the site electrical survey. Confirm bollard/vehicle protection is installed per site risk assessment. Confirm whether the optional 4G module was ordered, since this changes the connectivity commissioning steps.
properties.requiredTools: Pedestal lifting/positioning equipment, anchor bolt kit, torque wrench, cable pulling equipment, multimeter, insulation resistance tester, RCD/GFCI test instrument, spirit level, NMG installation bracket kit, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves connection to mains electrical supply. Installation and final connection must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or an NMG-certified installation technician, in compliance with local electrical codes. Obtain all required electrical work permits before starting. Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) on the upstream distribution board before opening any enclosure. Wear appropriate PPE (insulated gloves, safety glasses, arc-rated clothing where applicable). Do not proceed with commissioning until post-installation continuity, insulation resistance, and RCD/GFCI trip testing have been completed and recorded.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Confirm foundation anchor bolt positions match the NX-200 template and isolate the supply circuit with lockout/tagout applied. 2. Position and secure the pedestal onto the foundation anchors, torquing to the specified value. 3. Route supply cabling through the foundation conduit into the pedestal's connection compartment and terminate per the wiring diagram. 4. Connect Ethernet, and if ordered, install and connect the optional 4G module per its addendum. 5. Close and secure all access panels. 6. Restore power only after the electrician confirms terminations and torque values are correct. 7. Power on and confirm the display reaches a steady 'ready' state.
properties.validation: Perform and record continuity, insulation resistance, and RCD/GFCI trip tests. Confirm pedestal is mechanically stable (no movement under lateral load test). Confirm the unit registers in Polaris and reports 'Available'. If the 4G module is installed, confirm signal strength and successful backend heartbeat over cellular as a connectivity fallback path. Perform a test charge session and confirm correct metering and RFID card authorization if RFID commissioning has been completed.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If the pedestal shows movement after torquing, stop work and re-inspect the foundation before proceeding — do not compensate with additional shims alone. If Ethernet link is down, check patch cabling and switch port status before assuming a unit fault. If the 4G module fails to register, confirm SIM activation status with Polaris support before replacing hardware.
properties.escalation: Escalate foundation or civil-works nonconformance to the site project manager. Escalate persistent connectivity failures to NMG Field Engineering, referencing the site ID and serial number.
properties.tags: installation, NX-200, pedestal, foundation, AC charger, 4G optional

properties.title: NX-400 Dual Charger Installation Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the standard installation procedure for the Nova AC 400 (NX-400), a 2x22 kW dual-socket wall or pedestal-mounted charger intended for large corporate or public parking deployments with integrated 4G, OCPP 2.0.1 connectivity, and dynamic load balancing.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the site electrical survey has sized the supply circuit for the full 2x22 kW dual-socket load, accounting for any dynamic load-balancing group the unit will join. Confirm mounting surface or foundation is complete and rated for the NX-400's weight. Confirm the Ethernet drop is available at the mounting location — Ethernet is the primary connectivity path, with integrated 4G as standard fallback. Confirm whether this unit will participate in a load-balancing group with other NX-400/450 units at the site, as this affects commissioning sequence.
properties.requiredTools: Mounting/anchor kit appropriate to wall or pedestal configuration, torque wrench, cable pulling and termination tools, multimeter, insulation resistance tester, RCD/GFCI test instrument, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app, laptop with OCPP diagnostic client (optional).
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves connection to mains electrical supply. Installation and final connection must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or an NMG-certified installation technician, in compliance with local electrical codes. Obtain all required electrical work permits before starting. Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) on the upstream distribution board before opening any enclosure. Wear appropriate PPE (insulated gloves, safety glasses, arc-rated clothing where applicable). Do not proceed with commissioning until post-installation continuity, insulation resistance, and RCD/GFCI trip testing have been completed and recorded. Both socket circuits must be verified independently before energizing given the dual-socket configuration.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Isolate and lockout/tagout the supply circuit(s) feeding both sockets. 2. Mount the unit per the wall or pedestal template, as applicable. 3. Route and terminate supply cabling for both sockets per the wiring diagram, verifying conductor sizing matches the site survey. 4. Connect the Ethernet cable; the integrated 4G module requires no separate hardware step but should be confirmed active during commissioning. 5. Close and secure enclosure panels. 6. Restore power only after the electrician confirms terminations on both circuits. 7. Power on and confirm both sockets reach a steady 'ready' state independently.
properties.validation: Perform and record continuity, insulation resistance, and RCD/GFCI trip tests on both socket circuits independently. Confirm the unit registers with Polaris over OCPP 2.0.1 and reports both sockets as 'Available'. Perform a test charge session on each socket sequentially and confirm independent metering. If part of a load-balancing group, confirm via the Load-Balancing Commissioning procedure before releasing the site to the customer.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If one socket fails post-installation testing while the other passes, isolate and re-test that circuit independently before assuming a full unit fault. If OCPP registration fails, confirm the unit's OCPP 2.0.1 endpoint configuration and Ethernet link before escalating. Note that E217 (intermittent OCPP disconnect after ~72h uptime) is a known firmware 4.8 issue, fixed in 4.8.1 — confirm firmware version if this symptom appears post-commissioning.
properties.escalation: Escalate persistent per-socket electrical test failures to the electrician of record and NMG Field Engineering. Escalate OCPP registration failures that persist after Ethernet and endpoint checks to the Polaris integration team.
properties.tags: installation, NX-400, dual-socket, OCPP 2.0.1, load balancing, 4G

properties.title: NX-450 Installation and Plug & Charge Certificate Provisioning Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the installation procedure for the Nova AC 450 (NX-450), the premium successor to the NX-400 released March 2026. The base mechanical and electrical installation is identical to the NX-400 procedure; this document adds the additional Plug & Charge certificate provisioning step unique to the NX-450, which the NX-400 does not support.
properties.prerequisites: All prerequisites listed in the NX-400 Dual Charger Installation procedure apply identically to the NX-450 (site survey sizing for 2x22 kW dual-socket load, foundation/mounting readiness, Ethernet drop availability, load-balancing group planning). Additionally, confirm the site has an active Plug & Charge contract provisioning entitlement in Polaris before beginning certificate provisioning.
properties.requiredTools: Same tools as the NX-400 installation procedure, plus a laptop or mobile device with access to the Polaris Plug & Charge certificate provisioning module.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves connection to mains electrical supply. Installation and final connection must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or an NMG-certified installation technician, in compliance with local electrical codes. Obtain all required electrical work permits before starting. Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) on the upstream distribution board before opening any enclosure. Wear appropriate PPE (insulated gloves, safety glasses, arc-rated clothing where applicable). Do not proceed with commissioning until post-installation continuity, insulation resistance, and RCD/GFCI trip testing have been completed and recorded. These requirements are identical to the NX-400 installation for the mechanical/electrical portion of this procedure.
properties.procedureSteps: 1-7. Perform the mechanical mounting and electrical connection steps identically to the NX-400 Dual Charger Installation procedure. 8. Once the unit registers with Polaris over OCPP 2.0.1, open the Plug & Charge provisioning module and initiate certificate issuance for the unit's OEM identity. 9. Confirm the unit downloads and installs its Plug & Charge root and leaf certificates successfully. 10. Perform a Plug & Charge test session with a compatible test vehicle or simulator to confirm certificate-based autonomous authentication and charging start, without RFID or app interaction.
properties.validation: Complete all NX-400 validation steps (continuity, insulation resistance, RCD/GFCI testing, per-socket metering test). Additionally, confirm the Plug & Charge certificate status shows 'Provisioned — Active' in Polaris, and confirm a successful autonomous Plug & Charge test session completes without manual authorization.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If certificate provisioning fails, confirm the site's Plug & Charge entitlement is active before retrying — a common cause is an unprovisioned contract at the account level rather than a device fault. If a Plug & Charge test session does not autonomously authenticate, confirm the vehicle or simulator is Plug & Charge-capable before treating this as a charger defect.
properties.escalation: Escalate certificate provisioning failures that persist after entitlement confirmation to the Polaris Plug & Charge support team, referencing the unit serial number and site account ID.
properties.tags: installation, NX-450, Plug and Charge, certificate provisioning, OCPP 2.0.1

properties.title: DX-60 DC Fast Charger Installation Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the standard installation procedure for the Nova DC 60 (DX-60), a 60 kW single-gun (CCS2) DC fast charger intended for retail and hotel sites.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the site electrical survey has sized and provisioned the three-phase 400V supply circuit for the DX-60's rated load. Confirm the concrete foundation pad is complete, cured, and meets the DX-60 footprint and clearance drawing. Confirm the CCS2 cable management and vehicle approach clearance meet the site layout drawing. Confirm the Ethernet drop is available; 4G is standard on this unit as a connectivity fallback.
properties.requiredTools: Lifting/positioning equipment rated for the DX-60 cabinet weight, anchor bolt kit, torque wrench, three-phase cable termination tools, multimeter, insulation resistance tester, RCD/residual current test instrument, clamp meter, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves connection to a three-phase mains electrical supply. Installation and final connection must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified DC fast-charger technician, in compliance with local electrical codes. Obtain all required electrical work permits and, where applicable, grid-operator connection approval before starting. Apply lockout/tagout on all three phases at the upstream distribution board. Wear PPE appropriate to three-phase work including arc-rated clothing where required by local code. Do not energize the unit until post-installation continuity, insulation resistance, and RCD testing are complete and documented.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Confirm foundation anchor positions and isolate/lockout-tagout the three-phase supply. 2. Position and secure the DX-60 cabinet onto the foundation. 3. Route and terminate the three-phase supply cable into the cabinet per the wiring diagram, verifying phase rotation. 4. Connect the CCS2 dispenser cable and confirm secure mechanical mounting of the cable management arm. 5. Connect Ethernet and confirm the integrated 4G module is active as fallback. 6. Close and secure all cabinet panels. 7. Restore power only after the electrician confirms correct phase rotation and torque values. 8. Power on and confirm the unit reaches a steady 'ready' state and the gun status shows 'Available'.
properties.validation: Perform and record continuity, insulation resistance, phase rotation, and RCD testing before energizing. Confirm the unit registers with Polaris over OCPP 2.0.1. Perform a test charge session with a CCS2-capable test vehicle or DC load simulator and confirm correct power delivery ramp and metering. Confirm the gun connector locks and releases correctly.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If phase rotation is incorrect, do not proceed with commissioning — correct at the distribution board before re-testing. If the unit powers on but the gun will not initiate a charge session, check the CCS2 connector interlock sensor and cable continuity before escalating. If OCPP registration fails, verify Ethernet link status first.
properties.escalation: Escalate phase rotation or supply sizing discrepancies to the electrician of record and the site's grid operator contact. Escalate persistent charge-session failures to NMG Field Engineering with the fault log exported from the unit.
properties.tags: installation, DX-60, DC fast charger, CCS2, three-phase

properties.title: DX-120 Commissioning Checklist (Paper Sign-Off, Legacy)
properties.purpose: SUPERSEDED — Legacy paper-based commissioning checklist for the Nova DC 120 (DX-120), used prior to 2025 to record commissioning test results and obtain a physical technician sign-off sheet. This procedure has been superseded by PROC-INSTALL-DX120-001, which replaces the paper form with a digital Polaris commissioning checklist. Retained for historical reference only; do not use for new installations.
properties.prerequisites: Same electrical and civil prerequisites as DX-120 commissioning generally: confirmed ~175A three-phase 400V supply, completed transformer/switchgear room access where applicable, and completed foundation works.
properties.requiredTools: Printed DX-120 Commissioning Checklist form (NMG-FORM-DX120-01), clipboard, multimeter, insulation resistance tester, RCD test instrument, clamp meter.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves connection to a three-phase mains electrical supply at approximately 175A. Installation and connection must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified DC fast-charger technician. Obtain all electrical permits and apply lockout/tagout before beginning work. Do not energize until all paper checklist test items are recorded as passed.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Complete mechanical and electrical installation per the standard DX-120 procedure. 2. Perform each test listed on the printed NMG-FORM-DX120-01 checklist in sequence, recording pass/fail by hand. 3. Obtain the site electrician's physical signature confirming electrical test results. 4. Obtain the commissioning technician's physical signature confirming functional test results. 5. Photograph the completed signed form and file it with the regional operations office within 5 business days. 6. Retain the original paper form on-site per the regional records policy.
properties.validation: The commissioning is considered valid only once the printed form is fully signed by both the electrician and the commissioning technician and filed with the regional office.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If the paper form is lost before filing, the commissioning must be re-performed and re-recorded — there is no digital backup under this legacy process, which was a key driver for retiring it in favor of PROC-INSTALL-DX120-001.
properties.escalation: Escalate missing or incomplete forms to the regional operations office.
properties.tags: commissioning, DX-120, legacy, paper checklist, superseded

properties.title: DX-120 Commissioning Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the current commissioning procedure for the Nova DC 120 (DX-120), a 120 kW 1-2 gun (CCS2) DC fast charger for corporate and retail hub sites requiring approximately 175A three-phase 400V supply. This procedure replaces the legacy paper-based checklist (PROC-INSTALL-DX120-OLDCHECK) with a digital Polaris commissioning workflow.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the site electrical survey has provisioned an approximately 175A three-phase 400V supply. Confirm the foundation, and where applicable, transformer/switchgear room access, meets the DX-120 site preparation drawing. Confirm the Ethernet drop is available with 4G as standard fallback. Confirm the commissioning technician has an active Polaris Field Installer app account with digital checklist access.
properties.requiredTools: Lifting/positioning equipment rated for the DX-120 cabinet, anchor bolt kit, torque wrench, three-phase cable termination tools, multimeter, insulation resistance tester, RCD test instrument, clamp meter, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app (digital commissioning checklist).
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves connection to a three-phase mains electrical supply. Installation and final connection must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified DC fast-charger technician, in compliance with local electrical codes. Obtain all required electrical work permits and, where applicable, grid-operator connection approval before starting. Apply lockout/tagout on all three phases at the upstream distribution board. Wear PPE appropriate to three-phase work including arc-rated clothing where required by local code. Do not energize the unit until post-installation continuity, insulation resistance, and RCD testing are complete and documented. Wear PPE appropriate to three-phase and higher-current DC fast-charger work.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Complete mechanical mounting and three-phase supply termination per the DX-120 wiring diagram, verifying phase rotation. 2. Connect CCS2 gun(s), Ethernet, and confirm 4G fallback is active. 3. Open the Polaris Field Installer app's digital DX-120 commissioning checklist and begin recording each electrical test result directly into the app as it is performed. 4. Restore power only after the electrician confirms terminations and phase rotation. 5. Power on and confirm each gun reaches a steady 'ready' state. 6. Complete the digital checklist's functional test section, including a live test charge session per gun.
properties.validation: Confirm continuity, insulation resistance, phase rotation, and RCD test results are recorded and pass within the digital checklist. Confirm the unit registers with Polaris over OCPP 2.0.1 and each gun independently reports 'Available'. Confirm a completed test charge session per gun with correct metering. The digital checklist auto-files to the regional operations record on submission, removing the paper-loss risk of the legacy process.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If the digital checklist fails to submit, confirm the technician's device has network connectivity before re-attempting — do not proceed to energize a second gun until the first gun's results have submitted successfully. If phase rotation is incorrect, correct at the distribution board before continuing.
properties.escalation: Escalate supply sizing or phase rotation issues to the electrician of record. Escalate persistent digital checklist submission failures to the Polaris support team.
properties.tags: commissioning, DX-120, DC fast charger, digital checklist, three-phase

properties.title: DX-240 Commissioning Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the commissioning procedure for the Nova DC 240 (DX-240), a modular 240 kW (2x120kW), 2-4 gun (CCS2) DC fast charger for logistics hub sites. Installation prerequisites and commissioning steps closely resemble the DX-120 procedure, but the DX-240 requires an approximately 350A three-phase 400V supply — roughly double the DX-120's ~175A requirement — reflecting its modular dual-120kW power architecture.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the site electrical survey has provisioned an approximately 350A three-phase 400V supply — verify this explicitly, since undersizing based on a DX-120-style ~175A assumption is a common site-survey error for this product. Confirm the dedicated transformer/switchgear room and cable routing meet the DX-240 site preparation drawing, which resembles the DX-120's but is sized for the higher current rating. Confirm the Ethernet drop is available with 4G as standard fallback. Confirm the commissioning technician has an active Polaris Field Installer app account.
properties.requiredTools: Lifting/positioning equipment rated for the DX-240 cabinet(s), anchor bolt kit, torque wrench, three-phase cable termination tools rated for the higher current, clamp meter rated for the expected current draw, multimeter, insulation resistance tester, RCD test instrument, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves connection to a three-phase mains electrical supply at approximately 350A — a substantially higher current than the DX-60/DX-120. Installation and connection must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified DC fast-charger technician with high-current commissioning experience. Obtain all electrical permits and grid-operator approvals before starting. Apply lockout/tagout across all three phases and confirm zero-energy state with a rated voltage detector before opening any enclosure. Arc-flash PPE is required per the site's arc-flash risk assessment given the higher available fault current at this supply rating. Do not energize until continuity, insulation resistance, and RCD testing are complete and recorded.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Confirm the ~350A three-phase supply matches the site survey and isolate/lockout-tagout all phases. 2. Position and secure the modular DX-240 cabinet(s) per the foundation drawing. 3. Route and terminate the three-phase supply cable using conductors and terminations rated for 350A, verifying phase rotation — this step follows the same sequence as DX-120 commissioning but with higher-rated cabling and torque specifications. 4. Connect CCS2 guns, Ethernet, and confirm 4G fallback. 5. Restore power only after the electrician confirms terminations, torque values, and phase rotation at the higher current rating. 6. Power on both 120kW modules and confirm each reaches a steady 'ready' state independently. 7. Complete the digital Polaris commissioning checklist, recording each electrical and functional test.
properties.validation: Confirm continuity, insulation resistance, phase rotation, and RCD test results at the 350A supply rating. Confirm both modules register with Polaris over OCPP 2.0.1 and each gun reports 'Available' independently. Confirm a test charge session per gun with correct metering and correct power-sharing behavior between the two 120kW modules when multiple guns are active simultaneously.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If one 120kW module fails to register while the other succeeds, isolate and re-test that module's supply termination independently — this mirrors the DX-120 module fault-isolation approach at higher current. If overcurrent protection trips during initial energization, verify the supply sizing against the site survey before assuming a unit defect; do not simply reset the breaker without confirming supply capacity.
properties.escalation: Escalate supply undersizing (common when a DX-120-style ~175A assumption was used in error) to the site project manager and electrician of record immediately, as this requires a civil/electrical rework, not a device-level fix. Escalate persistent module registration failures to NMG Field Engineering.
properties.tags: commissioning, DX-240, DC fast charger, three-phase, 350A, modular

properties.title: DX-360 Site Preparation Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the site preparation procedure for the Nova DC 360 (DX-360), a modular 360 kW (3x120kW), 2-6 gun (CCS2) DC fast charger for logistics hub and highway locations, which requires a dedicated MV/LV substation above approximately 400A. This procedure covers civil and electrical infrastructure readiness ahead of the mechanical/electrical commissioning steps.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the site has completed a dedicated MV/LV substation design review sized above ~400A supply, coordinated with the local grid/distribution network operator. In Belgium, coordinate substation connection applications with Elia (the Belgian transmission system operator) or the relevant regional distribution operator (Fluvius/ORES/Sibelga depending on region); typical connection study lead times for a >400A connection in Belgium can exceed six months and must be factored into project scheduling from the outset. Confirm long-lead-time civil works (foundation, cable trenching, transformer room construction) are scheduled with sufficient lead time given substation approval timelines. Confirm the site layout drawing accounts for 2-6 gun vehicle approach and queuing for logistics/highway traffic patterns.
properties.requiredTools: Site survey instrumentation, civil works coordination documentation, grid-operator connection application forms, cable route marking equipment.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure covers pre-energization site preparation for a dedicated MV/LV substation exceeding ~400A. All substation design, grid-operator coordination, and eventual energization must be performed by, or under the direct supervision of, a qualified/licensed electrician or engineering firm accredited for MV/LV substation work, in coordination with the local grid operator. Do not attempt any live electrical work under this procedure — it is a pre-construction planning and readiness document only.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Submit the MV/LV substation connection application to the local grid/distribution network operator (Elia/Fluvius/ORES/Sibelga in Belgium, or the equivalent local DSO elsewhere), referencing the site's projected ~400A+ demand. 2. Coordinate civil works scheduling (foundation, trenching, transformer room) around the grid operator's approval and construction timeline. 3. Confirm cable routing between the substation and each DX-360 cabinet location meets separation and derating requirements for the expected current. 4. Confirm foundation pads for the modular cabinet(s) are complete and cured per the DX-360 drawing. 5. Confirm site layout supports 2-6 gun vehicle circulation without conflicting with substation access requirements. 6. Once civil and substation works are complete, hand off to the DX-240/DX-120-style commissioning sequence, adapted for the DX-360's three-module (3x120kW) configuration, for final electrical connection and commissioning.
properties.validation: Confirm grid-operator substation approval and energization date are confirmed in writing. Confirm foundation and cable routing works pass civil inspection. Confirm the substation's protection settings are coordinated with the DX-360's expected load profile before scheduling commissioning.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If grid-operator approval is delayed, do not schedule commissioning technicians until a confirmed energization date is received — this is the most common cause of wasted site visits for DX-360 deployments, particularly in Belgium given typical connection study lead times. If foundation or trenching civil inspection fails, resolve before proceeding to cable pulling.
properties.escalation: Escalate grid-operator delays or substation design questions to the NMG major-account infrastructure team. Escalate civil inspection failures to the site's general contractor and project manager.
properties.tags: site preparation, DX-360, substation, MV/LV, logistics hub, Belgium, Elia

properties.title: Ethernet Network Configuration Procedure (All Connected Units)
properties.purpose: Describes the generic procedure for configuring wired Ethernet network connectivity on any NMG connected charging unit (NX-100 through DX-360), establishing the primary communication path to the Polaris Charge Cloud backend.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm a live Ethernet drop with DHCP or static IP allocation available at the unit's install location, per the site network survey. Confirm firewall rules permit outbound connectivity from the unit to the Polaris backend endpoints on the required ports. Confirm VLAN assignment, if applicable, has been communicated by the customer's IT team.
properties.requiredTools: Ethernet cable tester, laptop with network diagnostic tools, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves only low-voltage network cabling and does not require mains electrical isolation on its own; however, if network termination work requires opening a unit's electrical compartment, treat that step under the applicable product's mains electrical safety warnings and involve a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician as required.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Terminate and test the Ethernet cable using a cable tester to confirm correct pinout and link integrity. 2. Connect the cable to the unit's network port. 3. On the unit's local configuration interface (via the Polaris Field Installer app or the unit's local web UI, depending on model), confirm DHCP is enabled, or enter the static IP configuration provided by the site network survey. 4. Confirm the unit obtains an IP address and can reach the Polaris backend endpoint (ping/traceroute or the app's built-in connectivity check). 5. Confirm the unit registers with Polaris and reports a healthy heartbeat.
properties.validation: Confirm the unit shows 'Online' status in Polaris within 5 minutes of connection. Confirm no E204 (Ethernet connectivity failure) or E101 (heartbeat lost) errors are logged during a 15-minute observation window.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If the link light does not illuminate, re-test the cable and check the switch port status before assuming a unit-side fault. If the unit obtains an IP but cannot reach Polaris, confirm outbound firewall rules with the customer's IT team — this is the most common cause of E204/E101 errors post-installation. If 4G is present as fallback, confirm whether the unit failed over to cellular, which can mask an underlying Ethernet misconfiguration.
properties.escalation: Escalate persistent firewall or VLAN misconfiguration issues to the customer's IT team with the required Polaris endpoint/port list. Escalate suspected unit-side network hardware faults to NMG Field Engineering.
properties.tags: Ethernet, network configuration, connectivity, generic, all products

properties.title: 4G Cellular Connectivity Commissioning Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for commissioning 4G cellular connectivity as a backend communication path. On the NX-200 this is an optional add-on module; on the NX-400, NX-450, and all DX-series units, integrated 4G ships as standard, typically used as a resilient fallback to the primary Ethernet connection. This procedure's SIM activation section describes the legacy phone-based carrier activation workflow and is marked deprecated: SIM activation is being migrated to the Polaris self-service SIM provisioning portal. The physical commissioning and validation steps below remain accurate; refer to current Polaris account provisioning guidance for the activation step specifically until an updated procedure is published.
properties.prerequisites: For the NX-200, confirm the optional 4G module was ordered and physically installed per its hardware addendum before beginning this procedure. For NX-400/450 and DX-series units, confirm the integrated 4G module and its associated SIM are present (standard on these models). Confirm cellular coverage at the site meets the minimum signal strength requirement in the product's TechSpec sheet.
properties.requiredTools: Mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app, signal strength meter or the app's built-in signal diagnostic, SIM activation reference (site account ID).
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves only low-voltage module and antenna work. If module installation requires opening a unit's electrical compartment (NX-200 add-on case), treat that step under the NX-200 mains electrical safety warnings and involve a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician as required.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Confirm the SIM associated with the unit's serial number is activated against the site account in Polaris. 2. Power on the unit and allow the cellular modem to register with the carrier network. 3. Using the Polaris Field Installer app, confirm signal strength meets the minimum threshold; reposition the antenna or unit if signal is marginal. 4. Confirm the unit establishes a backend heartbeat over cellular — for units with Ethernet as primary, temporarily disconnect Ethernet to confirm cellular failover behaves correctly, then reconnect Ethernet. 5. Confirm the unit correctly reports its active connectivity path (Ethernet vs. cellular) in Polaris.
properties.validation: Confirm the unit registers with Polaris over cellular within 5 minutes. For fallback-configured units, confirm the unit correctly switches to cellular within the expected failover window when Ethernet is disconnected, and reverts to Ethernet when reconnected, without dropping an active session where testable. Confirm no E607 (4G/cellular modem connection failure) errors are logged during a 15-minute observation window.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If the modem fails to register, confirm SIM activation status in Polaris before assuming a hardware fault — an inactive SIM is the most common cause. If signal strength is below threshold, consider an external antenna kit where supported before escalating as a coverage gap. E607 errors that persist after confirming SIM activation and signal strength should be treated as a modem hardware issue.
properties.escalation: Escalate SIM activation issues to the Polaris account provisioning team. Escalate persistent E607 errors after activation and signal checks to NMG Field Engineering for modem replacement assessment.
properties.tags: 4G, cellular, connectivity, SIM, fallback, deprecated

properties.title: RFID Access Commissioning Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for commissioning RFID card-based authorization on NMG chargers that support it (NX-200, NX-400, NX-450, and all DX-series units — RFID is not available on the NX-100).
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the target unit supports RFID per the product capability matrix (NX-200/400/450, DX-60/120/240/360 — not NX-100). Confirm the site's RFID card population or a test card set is available. Confirm the unit has successfully completed Ethernet or 4G connectivity commissioning, since RFID authorization validation depends on backend connectivity to Polaris.
properties.requiredTools: Test RFID cards (valid and a deliberately invalid/deactivated card for negative testing), mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app, RFID reader cleaning cloth.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves only low-voltage reader hardware and does not require mains electrical isolation.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Confirm the RFID reader is present and free of visible damage or debris; clean the reader face if necessary. 2. In Polaris, confirm the unit's RFID reader is correctly linked to the site's card management group. 3. Present a valid, provisioned test card to the reader and confirm the unit authorizes and, where testable, initiates a charge session. 4. Present a deliberately invalid or deactivated test card and confirm the unit correctly rejects it (E117) and displays an appropriate rejection indication. 5. Confirm both authorization and rejection events are correctly logged in Polaris with the correct card identifier.
properties.validation: Confirm at least one successful authorization and one correct rejection (E117) are recorded in Polaris during commissioning. Confirm the reader responds within the expected read time (per the TechSpec sheet) without requiring repeated card presentation.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If a valid card is rejected, confirm the card is correctly provisioned and assigned to the site's card group in Polaris before treating this as a reader fault. If read reliability is poor (requires multiple presentations), clean the reader face and check for RF interference sources near the unit before escalating.
properties.escalation: Escalate card provisioning/group assignment issues to the customer's Polaris account administrator. Escalate persistent reader hardware read failures after cleaning to NMG Field Engineering.
properties.tags: RFID, access commissioning, card authorization, E117

properties.title: OCPP Backend Registration Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for registering a charging unit's OCPP connection with the Polaris Charge Cloud backend. NX-400, NX-450, and all DX-series units use OCPP 2.0.1; NX-100 and NX-200 use OCPP 1.6J. The registration steps differ slightly by protocol version, as described below.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the unit has completed Ethernet or 4G connectivity commissioning. Confirm the unit's OCPP identity (charge point ID) has been pre-provisioned in Polaris against the site account before attempting registration. Confirm the correct OCPP protocol version is expected for the product model being commissioned (OCPP 1.6J for NX-100/200; OCPP 2.0.1 for NX-400/450 and all DX-series).
properties.requiredTools: Mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app, laptop with an OCPP diagnostic client (optional, for advanced troubleshooting).
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves only backend software configuration and does not require mains electrical isolation.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Confirm the unit's charge point ID and OCPP protocol version are correctly pre-provisioned in Polaris. 2. On the unit, confirm the OCPP backend URL and security credentials (for OCPP 2.0.1, this includes the required TLS/security profile; OCPP 1.6J on NX-100/200 uses the applicable legacy security profile) are correctly configured, typically pre-set at manufacture but verified during commissioning. 3. Restart the unit's OCPP client (via power cycle or the Field Installer app's remote restart function) to force a fresh BootNotification. 4. Confirm in Polaris that a BootNotification was received and accepted, and the unit's status transitions to 'Available'. 5. For OCPP 2.0.1 units, confirm the unit accepts a test remote-start/remote-stop transaction command; for OCPP 1.6J units, confirm the equivalent RemoteStartTransaction/RemoteStopTransaction behavior.
properties.validation: Confirm the unit shows 'Registered' and 'Available' status in Polaris. Confirm a successful remote start/stop command round-trip. Confirm no repeated BootNotification rejections are logged, which would indicate a credential or protocol-version mismatch.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If BootNotification is rejected, confirm the charge point ID and protocol version configured on the unit exactly match what was provisioned in Polaris — a protocol-version mismatch (e.g. a unit configured for 1.6J attempting to register against a 2.0.1-provisioned identity) is a common cause. On NX-400 units running firmware 4.8, be aware of E217 (intermittent OCPP disconnect after ~72h uptime, fixed in 4.8.1) if disconnects appear only after extended runtime rather than at initial registration.
properties.escalation: Escalate persistent BootNotification rejections after confirming protocol version and credentials to the Polaris integration team. Escalate suspected E217 occurrences on NX-400 firmware 4.8 by confirming firmware version and recommending upgrade to 4.8.1 per the Remote Firmware Update procedure.
properties.tags: OCPP, OCPP 2.0.1, OCPP 1.6J, backend registration, Polaris

properties.title: Dynamic Load-Balancing Commissioning Procedure (NX-400/NX-450)
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for commissioning dynamic load balancing across a group of two or more NX-400 and/or NX-450 units sharing a common circuit budget at a site. Dynamic load balancing is supported on NX-400 and NX-450 only — it is not available on NX-100, NX-200, or any DX-series unit.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm all units in the intended load-balancing group have completed individual electrical installation and OCPP backend registration. Confirm the shared circuit's total available capacity has been correctly specified in the site electrical survey. Confirm all units in the group are on compatible firmware versions supporting dynamic load balancing.
properties.requiredTools: Mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app, laptop with access to the Orion Energy Manager or Polaris load-balancing configuration module as applicable to the site's deployment.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure is a software/backend configuration step performed after all group units have completed individual electrical commissioning under their own installation procedures, each of which required a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician for the mains connection. No additional live electrical work is performed under this procedure.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. In Polaris, create or confirm the load-balancing group and add all participating NX-400/450 units by serial number. 2. Configure the shared circuit's total current/power budget per the site electrical survey. 3. Configure the group's allocation policy (equal-share, priority-based, or first-come-first-served, per the site's operational requirements). 4. Initiate simultaneous test charge sessions on at least two units in the group and confirm the total combined power draw does not exceed the configured circuit budget. 5. Confirm each unit correctly reports its dynamically allocated power limit during the concurrent test.
properties.validation: Confirm the group's combined power draw during the concurrent test session remains within the configured budget throughout, with no E301 (circuit breaker trip / overcurrent) events. Confirm each unit's allocated power adjusts correctly when a third session is started or an existing session ends.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If combined draw exceeds budget during testing, verify the circuit budget configuration matches the actual site electrical survey value before assuming a software defect. If an E315 (dynamic load-balancing conflict) error appears, confirm no duplicate or overlapping group configuration exists for the same circuit.
properties.escalation: Escalate persistent E315 conflicts or budget configuration mismatches to the Polaris integration team with the group configuration export. Escalate any observed overcurrent event (E301) to the electrician of record immediately and do not resume group operation until the circuit capacity is reconfirmed.
properties.tags: load balancing, NX-400, NX-450, dynamic allocation, E315, E301

properties.title: Orion Energy Manager Integration Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for integrating a site's charging infrastructure with Orion Energy Manager, NMG's dynamic energy management platform covering building load balancing, solar generation awareness, battery storage integration, and charging priority rules such as prioritizing fleet vehicles over visitor vehicles.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm all chargers at the site are registered and 'Available' in Polaris before beginning Orion integration. Confirm the site's building energy meter or sub-meter data feed is available and compatible with Orion's supported meter interfaces. Confirm the Orion Energy Manager tenant has been provisioned for the site account. If the site has solar generation or battery storage, confirm those systems' data interfaces are available (Orion 3.1+ adds solar-aware priority rules; Orion 3.2+ adds battery storage integration).
properties.requiredTools: Laptop with access to the Orion Energy Manager configuration console, building meter interface documentation, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure is a software/backend integration step. If building meter or sub-meter wiring work is required to establish the data feed, that specific step must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician, following standard lockout/tagout and PPE practice for the panel being accessed.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Link the site's Polaris charger fleet to the Orion Energy Manager tenant. 2. Configure the building energy meter data feed and confirm Orion receives live demand readings. 3. Configure the site's overall demand cap and, if applicable, peak-demand management rules. 4. If solar generation is present, configure solar-generation-aware charging priority rules (Orion 3.1+). 5. If battery storage is present, configure battery dispatch and charge-priority interaction rules (Orion 3.2+). 6. Configure charging priority rules — for example, prioritizing company/fleet vehicles over visitor vehicles, if required by the site's operating policy. 7. Run a test scenario exercising at least two priority tiers and confirm Orion correctly reallocates available power.
properties.validation: Confirm Orion receives a live, correctly-scaled meter reading. Confirm the test priority scenario correctly reallocates power to the higher-priority vehicle group when total demand exceeds the site's demand cap. Confirm no unexpected E301 (overcurrent) or E315 (load-balancing conflict) events occur during the test.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If Orion does not receive meter data, confirm the meter interface configuration and data feed connectivity before assuming a platform fault. If priority reallocation does not behave as configured, review the priority rule ordering — rule precedence errors are a common cause of unexpected allocation results.
properties.escalation: Escalate meter interface connectivity issues to the site's building management/electrical team. Escalate priority-rule configuration issues that persist after review to the Orion Energy Manager support team.
properties.tags: Orion Energy Manager, integration, load balancing, solar, battery storage, priority rules

properties.title: Polaris Charge Cloud Tenant Onboarding Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for onboarding a new customer site or account as a tenant within Polaris Charge Cloud, NMG's central charging infrastructure management platform, covering Device Management, Driver Management, Billing, Monitoring, Remote Diagnostics, Reporting, and API Management module activation as applicable to the customer's contracted service tier.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the customer contract specifies which Polaris modules are included (Device Management and Monitoring are always included; Billing, Remote Diagnostics, Reporting, and API Management are contract-dependent). Confirm the site's legal entity, billing details, and administrator contact have been collected. Confirm charger serial numbers to be commissioned at the site are known in advance where possible, to allow pre-provisioning.
properties.requiredTools: Access to the Polaris tenant administration console, customer contract and site details, laptop.
properties.safetyWarnings: This is a purely administrative/software onboarding procedure and involves no electrical work.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Create the new tenant record in Polaris with the customer's legal entity and site details. 2. Activate the contracted module set (Device Management, Driver Management, Billing, Monitoring, Remote Diagnostics, Reporting, API Management) per the signed contract. 3. Create the tenant administrator account and issue initial credentials. 4. Pre-provision known charger serial numbers against the tenant, ready for field commissioning. 5. If API Management is contracted (available since Polaris 2025.1, which also added OAuth2 client credentials support), configure the tenant's API credentials and scope entitlements. 6. Configure the tenant's driver/card management group structure if Driver Management is active. 7. Send onboarding confirmation and initial login instructions to the customer administrator.
properties.validation: Confirm the tenant administrator can log in and see the correct set of activated modules. Confirm at least one pre-provisioned charger serial number appears correctly associated with the tenant, ready to register once commissioned. If API Management is active, confirm a test OAuth2 client credentials token request succeeds.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If a contracted module does not appear active, confirm the tenant's service tier configuration against the signed contract before escalating as a platform fault — this is most often a data-entry mismatch at tenant creation. If OAuth2 token requests fail, confirm the tenant is on Polaris 2025.1 or later, since API Management with OAuth2 client credentials support was introduced in that release.
properties.escalation: Escalate contract/module mismatches to the NMG account management team. Escalate platform-level onboarding failures to Polaris platform support.
properties.tags: Polaris, tenant onboarding, Device Management, Billing, API Management, OAuth2

properties.title: Atlas Fleet Vehicle Enrollment Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for enrolling fleet vehicles into Atlas Fleet, NMG's fleet management and EV charging optimization platform, enabling route-aware charge scheduling, depot capacity forecasting, and driver mobile app access.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the customer's Atlas Fleet tenant has been provisioned (typically alongside or after Polaris tenant onboarding). Confirm the fleet vehicle list (identifiers, battery capacity, home depot assignment) is available from the customer. Confirm the depot's chargers are already registered in Polaris, since Atlas Fleet's depot capacity forecasting depends on live charger availability data.
properties.requiredTools: Access to the Atlas Fleet tenant administration console, fleet vehicle roster, laptop.
properties.safetyWarnings: This is a purely administrative/software enrollment procedure and involves no electrical work.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Create vehicle records in Atlas Fleet for each fleet vehicle, including battery capacity and home depot assignment. 2. Link each vehicle record to a driver account where the driver mobile app will be used. 3. Configure route-aware charge scheduling rules if the fleet has defined daily routes with return-to-depot charging needs (available since Atlas Fleet 2.1). 4. Configure depot capacity forecasting against the depot's registered charger count and capacity (available since Atlas Fleet 2.2). 5. If drivers will use the mobile app (Atlas Fleet 2.3 driver mobile app v2), issue driver app credentials and confirm at least one driver can log in and see their assigned vehicle.
properties.validation: Confirm each enrolled vehicle appears correctly in the fleet roster with the correct depot assignment. Confirm depot capacity forecasting produces a reasonable charging schedule recommendation given the enrolled fleet size and depot charger count. Confirm a test driver login to the mobile app succeeds and displays the correct assigned vehicle.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If depot capacity forecasting produces an implausible recommendation, confirm the depot's charger count and capacity data is correctly synced from Polaris before treating this as an Atlas Fleet defect. If a driver cannot log in to the mobile app, confirm the driver account was correctly linked to a vehicle record and that the account is on Atlas Fleet 2.3 or later for mobile app v2 features.
properties.escalation: Escalate depot/charger data sync issues to the Polaris integration team. Escalate persistent driver app login failures to Atlas Fleet platform support.
properties.tags: Atlas Fleet, vehicle enrollment, route-aware scheduling, depot forecasting, driver app

properties.title: DX-120 Installation — France Grid Connection Permit Procedure (Enedis)
properties.purpose: Describes the France-specific grid-connection permit procedure required before commissioning a DX-120 installation in France, in addition to the standard DX-120 Commissioning procedure. This procedure covers the Enedis (French distribution system operator) connection request and approval process specific to the ~175A three-phase supply the DX-120 requires.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the site's projected demand (~175A three-phase 400V) and installation address are finalized before submitting the Enedis connection request, since French grid connection applications require confirmed technical parameters. Confirm the customer or site owner has an active Enedis account or has authorized NMG to submit the connection request (Convention de Raccordement) on their behalf.
properties.requiredTools: Enedis connection request forms (Demande de Raccordement), site electrical survey, single-line diagram, proof of site ownership or occupancy authorization.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure covers the administrative grid-connection permit process only and involves no live electrical work. The eventual physical connection must still be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed French electrician (respecting NF C 15-100 and applicable French electrical code) or NMG-certified technician, following the standard DX-120 Commissioning procedure's electrical safety requirements once the Enedis connection is approved and energized.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Prepare and submit the Enedis Demande de Raccordement (connection request) with the site's confirmed technical parameters and single-line diagram. 2. Track the Enedis technical and financial proposal (Proposition de Raccordement) and confirm acceptance within the required timeframe. 3. Schedule the Enedis connection works (raccordement) date, which determines the earliest possible energization date for the site. 4. Once Enedis confirms energization, proceed with the standard DX-120 Commissioning procedure (PROC-INSTALL-DX120-001) for mechanical, electrical, and OCPP commissioning. 5. Retain the Enedis connection approval documentation in the site's permanent project file.
properties.validation: Confirm the Enedis Proposition de Raccordement was formally accepted and the connection works date is confirmed in writing before scheduling any on-site commissioning technician visit. Confirm the approved supply capacity matches or exceeds the ~175A three-phase requirement from the DX-120 site electrical survey.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If the Enedis proposal specifies a lower capacity than required, do not proceed to commissioning — resubmit with corrected technical parameters rather than attempting to commission against an undersized approved connection. If the connection works date slips, update the site project schedule before dispatching a commissioning technician, since technician visits scheduled ahead of a confirmed Enedis energization date are the most common cause of wasted site visits in France.
properties.escalation: Escalate Enedis proposal delays or capacity discrepancies to the NMG France infrastructure coordination team.
properties.tags: DX-120, France, Enedis, grid connection, permit, NF C 15-100

properties.title: Connector Inspection Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for inspecting charging connectors (Type 2 sockets on Nova AC units, CCS2 guns on Nova DC units) for wear, damage, and contact integrity, to be performed as part of routine maintenance or in response to a reported connector fault.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the unit is taken out of service (marked unavailable in Polaris) before beginning connector inspection to prevent a customer session starting mid-inspection.
properties.requiredTools: Visual inspection checklist, contact resistance meter or insulation tester as applicable, cleaning cloth, connector gauge tool (for pin/contact wear measurement), mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: Confirm the unit is de-energized at the connector/gun level (session ended, unit marked unavailable) before handling. If internal connector wiring inspection requires opening the unit's electrical compartment, this step must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician following standard lockout/tagout practice.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Mark the unit unavailable in Polaris. 2. Visually inspect the connector/gun body for cracks, discoloration, or physical damage. 3. Inspect pins/contacts for wear, pitting, or discoloration indicating overheating; measure contact wear against the connector gauge tool where applicable. 4. Inspect the connector cable and strain relief for damage, kinks, or exposed conductors. 5. Clean the connector face and pins per the manufacturer cleaning guidance. 6. For CCS2 guns, test the connector interlock/latch mechanism for correct engagement and release. 7. Reconnect and perform a test charge session to confirm correct connection detection and session start.
properties.validation: Confirm no visible damage or excessive contact wear beyond the gauge tolerance. Confirm the interlock/latch mechanism engages and releases correctly on CCS2 guns. Confirm a successful test charge session with correct connection detection.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If contact discoloration suggests overheating, do not return the connector to service without further investigation — this can indicate a loose termination inside the unit, not just connector wear. If the interlock mechanism does not engage reliably, replace the connector assembly rather than attempting field adjustment beyond the manufacturer-approved steps.
properties.escalation: Escalate any connector showing evidence of overheating or an unreliable interlock mechanism to NMG Field Engineering for a replacement decision.
properties.tags: connector inspection, CCS2, Type 2, wear, maintenance

properties.title: Cooling System Inspection Procedure (DC Fast Chargers)
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for inspecting the active cooling system (fans, liquid cooling loop where fitted, air filters/vents) on DC fast chargers (DX-60, DX-120, DX-240, DX-360), which rely on effective cooling to sustain rated power output.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the unit's recent operating temperature and fault history in Polaris. Confirm the unit can be taken out of service for the duration of the inspection.
properties.requiredTools: Filter cleaning/replacement kit, fan diagnostic tool or tachometer, thermal imaging camera (recommended for higher-power DX-240/360 modules), cleaning brushes, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure requires opening cooling system access panels, which may be adjacent to high-voltage compartments on DC fast chargers. This work must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified DC fast-charger technician. Apply lockout/tagout before opening any panel adjacent to power electronics. Allow the unit to cool to a safe handling temperature before inspection if it was recently in an active charging session.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Mark the unit unavailable in Polaris and allow it to cool if recently active. 2. Isolate and lockout/tagout the supply if the cooling system access panel is adjacent to power electronics. 3. Inspect and clean or replace air filters and vents per the maintenance schedule. 4. Confirm fan operation and rotational speed against the specified range using a tachometer; replace any fan outside tolerance. 5. On liquid-cooled modules (as applicable to DX-240/360's modular power electronics), inspect coolant level, hose condition, and check for leaks. 6. Optionally, perform a thermal imaging scan of the power electronics compartment during a subsequent test charge session to confirm even heat distribution and no hotspots. 7. Restore power and perform a test charge session, monitoring internal temperature readings in Polaris/the unit's diagnostic interface.
properties.validation: Confirm all fans operate within the specified speed range. Confirm no coolant leaks are present on liquid-cooled modules. Confirm internal temperature readings during the test charge session remain within the normal operating range specified in the TechSpec sheet, with no thermal-related fault codes.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If a fan is out of tolerance, replace it rather than attempting field repair. If coolant level is low, investigate for a leak before simply topping up, since undiagnosed slow leaks are the most common recurring cooling issue on modular DC units. If thermal imaging shows a hotspot on a specific module, isolate that module for further inspection before returning the full unit to service.
properties.escalation: Escalate any coolant leak or persistent thermal hotspot to NMG Field Engineering before returning the unit to full-power service — consider derating the affected module in Polaris in the interim if supported.
properties.tags: cooling system, DC fast charger, fans, thermal, maintenance

properties.title: NX-400 Firmware Update via USB
properties.purpose: SUPERSEDED — Describes the legacy procedure for updating NX-400 firmware locally using a technician's field laptop and a USB connection. This procedure has been superseded by PROC-MAINT-NX400-FWREMOTE, which performs firmware updates remotely through Polaris Charge Cloud and is now the preferred, standard method — this document is retained for historical reference and for the rare case where remote update is not possible (e.g. no network connectivity at all).
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the correct firmware package for the NX-400 has been downloaded to the technician's field laptop in advance, since USB updates require the file to be available locally. Confirm the unit can be safely taken out of service for the update window. Confirm the technician's laptop has the required NMG firmware update utility installed.
properties.requiredTools: Technician field laptop with the NMG firmware update utility and the correct firmware package, USB cable (type per the NX-400 service port), mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app for pre/post status checks.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure requires opening the NX-400's service access panel to reach the USB service port. This must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician, with the unit isolated from active charging sessions during the update. Do not disconnect the USB cable or power the unit off during an in-progress firmware transfer, as this can cause a failed/corrupted update (E512).
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Mark the unit unavailable in Polaris and confirm no active charging session is in progress. 2. Open the service access panel to reach the USB service port. 3. Connect the technician laptop via USB and launch the NMG firmware update utility. 4. Select the correct firmware package and initiate the transfer, monitoring progress and not interrupting the connection. 5. Once transfer completes, allow the unit to apply the update and reboot automatically. 6. Confirm the unit reports the new firmware version correctly. 7. Close and secure the service access panel and mark the unit available in Polaris.
properties.validation: Confirm the unit reports the target firmware version after reboot. Confirm the unit reconnects to Polaris and resumes 'Available' status. Perform a test charge session to confirm normal operation post-update.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If the transfer fails or the unit reports a checksum mismatch (E512), retry the full transfer from the beginning rather than attempting to resume a partial update. If the unit does not reboot correctly after update, do not power-cycle repeatedly — escalate for a possible recovery-mode procedure.
properties.escalation: Escalate any failed update that leaves the unit non-responsive after two clean retry attempts to NMG Field Engineering immediately, referencing the firmware package version attempted.
properties.tags: firmware update, USB, NX-400, superseded, legacy

properties.title: NX-400 Remote Firmware Update via Polaris
properties.purpose: Describes the current, preferred procedure for updating NX-400 firmware remotely through Polaris Charge Cloud, without requiring a technician site visit. This procedure supersedes PROC-MAINT-NX400-FWUSB, the legacy USB-based field-laptop update method, which remains available only as a fallback when a unit has no usable network connectivity.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the target unit is online and reporting a healthy heartbeat in Polaris before scheduling a remote update. Confirm the target firmware version is available in the Polaris firmware repository and has been validated for the unit's current firmware baseline (do not skip validated upgrade paths). Notify the site of a brief planned service interruption during the update window.
properties.requiredTools: Access to the Polaris Device Management module's remote firmware update function. No on-site tools or technician visit required for a successful remote update.
properties.safetyWarnings: This is a remote software procedure and involves no on-site electrical work under normal circumstances. If a remote update fails and requires an on-site recovery visit, that visit must be performed by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician following the unit's standard service-panel access safety requirements.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. In Polaris Device Management, select the target NX-400 unit(s) and the validated target firmware version. 2. Schedule the update for a low-traffic window and confirm the unit is marked unavailable for the duration. 3. Initiate the remote update and monitor transfer and application progress via the Polaris dashboard. 4. Confirm the unit reboots and reports the new firmware version. 5. Mark the unit available in Polaris and perform a remote test charge session validation if possible, or flag for a lightweight on-site spot-check per the site's maintenance schedule. 6. If updating past firmware 4.8, note that 4.8.1 specifically fixes E217 (intermittent OCPP backend disconnect after ~72h continuous uptime) — prioritize units still on 4.8 for update to at least 4.8.1.
properties.validation: Confirm the unit reports the target firmware version in Polaris post-update. Confirm the unit resumes 'Available' status and normal OCPP heartbeat behavior. For units previously affected by E217, confirm no recurrence after 72+ hours of continuous uptime post-update to 4.8.1 or later.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If a remote update fails to complete, Polaris will typically retain the unit on its prior working firmware version rather than leaving it in a partial state — confirm the reported version before retrying. If a unit becomes unresponsive after a remote update, escalate for an on-site USB recovery visit per PROC-MAINT-NX400-FWUSB's fallback procedure rather than repeatedly retrying the remote update.
properties.escalation: Escalate any unit left unresponsive after a remote update attempt to NMG Field Engineering for an on-site recovery visit.
properties.tags: firmware update, remote, Polaris, NX-400, E217, current

properties.title: General Preventive Maintenance Procedure (All Products)
properties.purpose: Describes the general preventive maintenance schedule and procedure applicable across the NMG charger portfolio, complementing the Annual Charger Inspection with a lighter-weight, more frequent check intended to catch issues between full annual inspections.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the unit's maintenance interval (typically quarterly, per the site's service plan) and review recent fault history in Polaris before the visit.
properties.requiredTools: Visual inspection checklist, cleaning materials, basic hand tools, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure is primarily non-intrusive (visual/functional checks). If any check reveals a need to open the electrical compartment, that step must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician following standard lockout/tagout practice.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Review Polaris fault history since the last visit. 2. Perform an external visual inspection for damage, corrosion, or vandalism. 3. Clean the display, connector area, and vents/filters as applicable. 4. Confirm signage, safety labeling, and any required customer-facing instructions remain legible and intact. 5. Perform a test charge session to confirm normal functional operation. 6. Log the visit outcome in Polaris, noting any items flagged for follow-up (e.g. deferred to the next Annual Charger Inspection).
properties.validation: Confirm the unit completes a test charge session without error. Confirm no new fault codes were introduced since the last visit that remain unresolved.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If a fault code from the recent history recurs during the visit, do not simply clear it — investigate per the relevant Known Issue or Support Article before closing out the visit. If physical damage beyond routine wear is found, flag for a dedicated inspection visit rather than attempting repair under this lightweight procedure.
properties.escalation: Escalate any finding requiring electrical work or replacement parts to the appropriate dedicated maintenance procedure or NMG Field Engineering.
properties.tags: preventive maintenance, general, quarterly, all products

properties.title: Remote Diagnostics Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for using the Polaris Remote Diagnostics module (available since Polaris 2024.3) to investigate a reported charger fault without an immediate on-site visit, reducing unnecessary truck rolls and speeding up root-cause identification.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the target unit is online in Polaris (Remote Diagnostics requires an active backend connection). Confirm the reporting fault code, symptom description, or customer complaint has been logged before beginning the remote session.
properties.requiredTools: Access to the Polaris Remote Diagnostics module.
properties.safetyWarnings: This is a remote, read-only diagnostic procedure and involves no on-site electrical work. Do not attempt to remotely trigger a live test charge session on a unit reported with a safety-relevant fault code (e.g. E301 overcurrent) without first assessing whether an on-site visit is safer.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Open the target unit's remote diagnostics session in Polaris. 2. Review the unit's recent fault code history, connectivity log, and firmware version. 3. Cross-reference any reported fault code against the relevant Known Issue and Support Article documentation. 4. If safe to do so, remotely query the unit's live status (temperature, session state, connectivity path) for further context. 5. Determine whether the issue can be resolved remotely (e.g. a remote restart, a configuration correction) or requires an on-site visit. 6. Log the diagnostic findings and resolution or escalation decision in Polaris.
properties.validation: Confirm the diagnostic session correctly retrieved the unit's fault history and live status. If a remote resolution action was taken (e.g. remote restart), confirm the fault clears and the unit returns to normal status.
