properties.procTroubleshooting: If the unit does not respond to a remote diagnostics query, this itself is diagnostic information (likely a connectivity issue such as E101/E204/E607) — proceed directly to on-site dispatch rather than repeating the remote query indefinitely.
properties.escalation: Escalate any fault that cannot be resolved or safely characterized remotely to an on-site maintenance visit, providing the field technician with the remote diagnostics findings in advance.
properties.tags: remote diagnostics, Polaris, Remote Diagnostics module, fault triage

properties.title: Replacing Communication Modules Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for replacing a faulty Ethernet, Wi-Fi, or 4G cellular communication module on an NMG charging unit, restoring backend connectivity to Polaris.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the specific communication module fault (e.g. persistent E204, E607) via remote diagnostics before dispatching a technician with the correct replacement part. Confirm the replacement module part number matches the unit's model and hardware revision.
properties.requiredTools: Replacement communication module (Ethernet/Wi-Fi/4G as applicable), anti-static handling equipment, torque screwdriver, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure requires opening the unit's electrical/communications compartment. This must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician. Isolate and lockout/tagout the supply before opening the compartment, even though the communication module itself is low-voltage, since it is typically located near power electronics.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Mark the unit unavailable in Polaris. 2. Isolate and lockout/tagout the supply and open the compartment housing the communication module. 3. Using anti-static precautions, disconnect and remove the faulty module. 4. Install the replacement module and reconnect per the wiring/connector diagram. 5. Close and secure the compartment and restore power. 6. Re-run the applicable connectivity commissioning procedure (Ethernet Configuration or 4G Cellular Module Commissioning) for the replaced module type. 7. Confirm the unit resumes normal backend connectivity in Polaris.
properties.validation: Confirm the unit re-establishes a healthy heartbeat with Polaris over the replaced module's connectivity path. Confirm the previously-reported fault code (E204/E607, etc.) no longer recurs during a 15-minute observation window.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If the fault persists after module replacement, verify the connector/wiring termination before assuming a second defective module — a poor connection is a more common cause than two consecutive faulty modules. If the replacement module is a different hardware revision, confirm compatibility before proceeding.
properties.escalation: Escalate persistent connectivity faults after module replacement and connection verification to NMG Field Engineering.
properties.tags: communication module, Ethernet, 4G, replacement, maintenance

properties.title: Charger Device Decommissioning Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for permanently decommissioning an NMG charging unit at end of life or upon customer removal request, covering safe electrical disconnection, backend deregistration, and data handling.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm decommissioning has been formally authorized by the site owner/customer. Confirm any outstanding billing or session data for the unit has been finalized in Polaris before deregistration.
properties.requiredTools: Standard electrical disconnection tools, multimeter, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app, disposal/recycling documentation per local e-waste regulations.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves final disconnection from mains electrical supply. This must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician. Apply lockout/tagout and confirm zero-energy state with a voltage detector before disconnecting supply conductors. Cap or terminate the abandoned supply circuit per local electrical code — do not leave live conductors exposed or unterminated.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Confirm authorization and finalize any outstanding Polaris billing/session records for the unit. 2. Mark the unit unavailable in Polaris and initiate the deregistration workflow. 3. Isolate and lockout/tagout the supply, then permanently disconnect and safely terminate/cap the supply conductors per local code. 4. Physically remove the unit from its mounting/foundation. 5. Deregister the unit's OCPP identity and remove it from any active load-balancing group or Orion Energy Manager configuration it participated in. 6. Handle disposal/recycling of the removed unit per local e-waste regulations, retaining disposal documentation. 7. Confirm the site's electrical single-line diagram is updated to reflect the removed load.
properties.validation: Confirm the unit no longer appears as an active device in Polaris. Confirm the abandoned circuit is correctly terminated and safe. Confirm any load-balancing group or Orion configuration referencing the removed unit has been updated to prevent orphaned references.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If the unit cannot be cleanly deregistered from Polaris due to unresolved billing records, resolve the billing record first rather than forcing deregistration, which can cause reporting discrepancies. If the unit was part of a load-balancing group, confirm the remaining group members' circuit budget is correctly recalculated after removal.
properties.escalation: Escalate unresolved billing/session record issues to the Polaris Billing support team. Escalate any load-balancing group recalculation issues to the Polaris integration team.
properties.tags: decommissioning, end of life, deregistration, disposal

properties.title: Polaris Tenant Health Review Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the periodic procedure for reviewing a customer tenant's overall health within Polaris Charge Cloud, covering device connectivity rates, open fault trends, billing reconciliation status, and module utilization, to proactively identify issues before they escalate to customer complaints.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm access to the tenant's Polaris administration console and, if applicable, the customer's most recent service plan tier (Essential/Professional/Gold) to benchmark expected response performance.
properties.requiredTools: Access to the Polaris tenant administration and Reporting module (Reporting module availability is contract-dependent per tenant).
properties.safetyWarnings: This is a purely administrative/reporting review procedure and involves no electrical or on-site work.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Review the tenant's overall device connectivity rate (percentage of devices online/reporting healthy heartbeat) over the review period. 2. Review open and recently-resolved fault trends across the tenant's device fleet, flagging any recurring fault code pattern. 3. Reconcile billing/session data completeness if the Billing module is active for the tenant. 4. Review module utilization (Device Management, Driver Management, Billing, Monitoring, Remote Diagnostics, Reporting, API Management) against the contracted entitlement to identify underused or over-limit modules. 5. Cross-check any Gold-tier customer's recent incident response times against the contracted SLA (including any applicable country-specific exception, e.g. Netherlands metro coverage limits, Spain's extended non-metro on-site window, or Germany's Bavaria/Baden-Wuerttemberg same-day exception) to confirm compliance. 6. Prepare a summary health report and flag any item requiring account management follow-up.
properties.validation: Confirm the health report accurately reflects the tenant's connectivity rate, fault trends, and SLA compliance status for the review period. Confirm any flagged SLA compliance concern is cross-checked against the correct country-specific exception before being reported as a breach.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If connectivity rate appears anomalously low, check for a shared root cause (e.g. a site-wide network outage) before treating it as many independent device faults. If an apparent SLA breach is found, re-verify against the applicable country exception (Netherlands/Spain/Germany) before escalating, since a standard-tier assumption is a common false-positive cause.
properties.escalation: Escalate confirmed SLA compliance concerns to the NMG account management team. Escalate systemic connectivity or fault trend anomalies to NMG Field Engineering.
properties.tags: Polaris, tenant health review, SLA, connectivity, reporting

properties.title: DC Fast-Charger Cable Management Inspection Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for inspecting the cable management arm/retraction system on DC fast chargers (DX-60/120/240/360), which supports the CCS2 dispenser cable and reduces strain and trip hazards. This paper-checklist-format procedure is marked deprecated: cable management inspection is being migrated into the Polaris digital field-app inspection workflow used for other maintenance procedures, but the technical inspection content below remains accurate and usable in the interim.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the unit can be taken out of service for the inspection duration.
properties.requiredTools: Visual inspection checklist (paper form, pending digital migration), cable tension/retraction test aid, cleaning materials, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app for status marking only.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure primarily involves mechanical inspection of the cable management arm and cable jacket. If the cable's electrical continuity must be tested at the connector end, treat that step under the applicable DC fast-charger's mains electrical safety warnings, requiring a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Mark the unit unavailable in Polaris. 2. Inspect the cable management arm's spring/counterweight or motorized retraction mechanism for smooth, controlled operation across its full range. 3. Inspect the dispenser cable jacket along its full length for cuts, abrasion, or exposed conductors, paying particular attention to the section nearest the connector and the section nearest the cabinet exit. 4. Confirm the cable does not drag on the ground or create a trip hazard at full extension under normal use. 5. Clean the cable jacket per manufacturer guidance. 6. Record findings on the paper checklist form and mark the unit available in Polaris.
properties.validation: Confirm the retraction mechanism operates smoothly without binding. Confirm no cable jacket damage exposing conductors is present.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If the retraction mechanism binds or operates roughly, do not lubricate as a first response — inspect for mechanical obstruction or wear first, since lubrication can mask a developing mechanical fault. If cable jacket damage is found, replace the cable assembly rather than field-repairing the jacket.
properties.escalation: Escalate any cable jacket damage exposing conductors, or a non-functional retraction mechanism, to NMG Field Engineering for a cable/arm replacement decision.
properties.tags: cable management, DC fast charger, inspection, deprecated, paper checklist

properties.title: RFID Reader Cleaning and Recalibration Procedure (Archived)
properties.purpose: Describes a now-archived procedure for cleaning and recalibrating RFID reader hardware using a specific cleaning solvent and a mechanical recalibration jig, both of which have since been discontinued by their manufacturers. This procedure is retained for historical reference only and does not apply to current RFID reader hardware revisions, which use a sealed, maintenance-free reader assembly requiring no field recalibration.
properties.prerequisites: Historical prerequisite: confirm availability of the NMG-approved cleaning solvent (product withdrawn) and the mechanical recalibration jig (no longer manufactured) before beginning this now-archived procedure.
properties.requiredTools: Historical tools, no longer stocked: NMG-approved RFID reader cleaning solvent (discontinued product), mechanical recalibration jig (discontinued), lint-free cloth.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves only low-voltage reader hardware and no mains electrical isolation. It is archived and should not be performed on current hardware; consult the current RFID Access Commissioning procedure (PROC-INSTALL-GEN-003) for any current-hardware reader issue instead.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. (Historical) Apply the NMG-approved cleaning solvent to a lint-free cloth and clean the reader face. 2. (Historical) Attach the mechanical recalibration jig and run the reader's recalibration sequence per the jig's instructions. 3. (Historical) Remove the jig and confirm read reliability with a test card. This entire sequence is retained for historical reference only — do not attempt to source the discontinued solvent or jig for current hardware.
properties.validation: Historical: confirm read reliability improved after recalibration. Not applicable to current sealed reader hardware.
properties.procTroubleshooting: For any current RFID reader issue, do not attempt this archived procedure — refer to the current RFID Access Commissioning procedure's troubleshooting section, which covers cleaning-face-only maintenance for the current sealed reader design.
properties.escalation: Not applicable — archived procedure. For a current RFID reader issue, escalate per the RFID Access Commissioning procedure.
properties.tags: RFID, reader cleaning, recalibration, archived, discontinued

properties.title: Backup Power (UPS) Check Procedure
properties.purpose: Describes the procedure for checking the health of an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) or backup power module fitted to units configured to retain control/communication power during a brief mains interruption, most commonly deployed on DC fast chargers at sites with critical uptime requirements.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the unit is configured with a UPS/backup power module per its site deployment record. Confirm the UPS's expected runtime and battery replacement interval per its specification.
properties.requiredTools: UPS diagnostic tool or the unit's built-in UPS status interface, multimeter, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure may require opening the unit's electrical compartment to access the UPS module. This must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician or NMG-certified technician. Apply lockout/tagout on the mains supply before working near the UPS module; note that the UPS battery itself may remain energized even with mains isolated — treat it as a live source until confirmed otherwise.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Mark the unit unavailable in Polaris if a UPS test requires simulating a mains interruption. 2. Check the UPS's reported battery health/state-of-charge via its diagnostic interface. 3. If within the test window of the maintenance schedule, safely simulate a brief mains interruption (per the UPS test procedure) and confirm the unit maintains control/communication power for the expected runtime. 4. Restore mains power and confirm the UPS correctly returns to standby/charging mode. 5. Record the battery health reading and test outcome in Polaris.
properties.validation: Confirm the UPS's reported battery health is within the manufacturer's acceptable range. Confirm the simulated interruption test, if performed, achieved the expected backup runtime without the unit losing communication with Polaris.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If battery health is degraded but the unit is not yet due for scheduled battery replacement, log the trend for early replacement planning rather than waiting for a full failure. If the unit loses communication during the simulated interruption test before the expected runtime, treat this as a failed test and do not rely on the UPS for its intended purpose until the battery is replaced.
properties.escalation: Escalate any UPS battery health reading below the acceptable threshold, or a failed interruption test, to NMG Field Engineering for battery replacement scheduling.
properties.tags: UPS, backup power, battery health, DC fast charger

properties.title: Load-Balancing Configuration Audit Procedure (NX-400/NX-450)
properties.purpose: Describes the periodic audit procedure for reviewing dynamic load-balancing group configurations across NX-400 and NX-450 units, confirming the configured circuit budget still matches actual site electrical capacity and that allocation policy remains appropriate for current site usage patterns.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm access to the load-balancing group's configuration in Polaris/Orion Energy Manager. Confirm the site's electrical survey has not been superseded by any subsequent site electrical work (e.g. added circuits, capacity upgrades) that would change the correct configured budget.
properties.requiredTools: Access to the Polaris/Orion load-balancing configuration console, the site's current electrical single-line diagram, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This is primarily a software configuration audit. If the audit reveals a need to physically re-verify site electrical capacity, that verification must be performed or directly supervised by a qualified/licensed electrician.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Review the load-balancing group's configured circuit budget against the site's current electrical single-line diagram. 2. Review recent E315 (load-balancing conflict) and E301 (overcurrent) event history for the group. 3. Review actual usage patterns (peak concurrent sessions, typical demand) against the configured allocation policy to confirm it remains appropriate (e.g. equal-share vs. priority-based). 4. If a discrepancy is found between configured budget and actual site capacity, correct the configuration and document the change. 5. Re-run a brief concurrent test session to confirm correct behavior after any configuration change.
properties.validation: Confirm the configured circuit budget matches the current site electrical capacity. Confirm no unresolved E315/E301 event pattern remains after any configuration correction. Confirm a post-audit concurrent test session behaves as expected.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If E315 events recur despite a correctly configured budget, review for a duplicate or conflicting group definition rather than assuming the budget value itself is wrong. If actual usage patterns have shifted significantly (e.g. new fleet vehicles added), recommend an allocation policy change rather than only adjusting the budget number.
properties.escalation: Escalate any confirmed mismatch between site electrical capacity and configured budget that requires a physical capacity change to the site's electrical contact and NMG Field Engineering.
properties.tags: load balancing, audit, NX-400, NX-450, E315, configuration review

properties.title: Annual Electrical Safety Re-Certification Procedure — Germany
properties.purpose: Describes the annual electrical safety re-certification procedure required for NMG charging installations in Germany, covering the periodic re-inspection and re-certification required under German electrical safety regulation, in addition to, and building on, the standard Annual Charger Inspection procedure.
properties.prerequisites: Confirm the unit's most recent electrical certification record and due date for re-certification. Confirm the assigned electrician holds the qualification required under German regulation (Elektrofachkraft, or equivalent recognized qualification) to perform and sign off the re-certification.
properties.requiredTools: German-standard electrical test instrumentation (insulation resistance tester, RCD/PRCD test instrument, loop impedance tester), the previous certification record, mobile device with the Polaris Field Installer app.
properties.safetyWarnings: This procedure involves mains electrical testing and must be performed or directly supervised by a suitably qualified electrician (Elektrofachkraft) in accordance with German electrical safety regulation (including VDE-based testing practice as applicable). Apply lockout/tagout before opening any electrical enclosure. Do not issue a re-certification unless all required tests pass and are documented; a failed re-certification result must be reported and the unit taken out of service until corrective action is completed.
properties.procedureSteps: 1. Complete the standard Annual Charger Inspection procedure's mechanical and visual checks. 2. Perform the full set of German-standard electrical safety tests (insulation resistance, RCD/PRCD trip time, loop impedance, protective conductor continuity) and record all results against the applicable German standard's pass thresholds. 3. Compare results against the previous certification record to identify any degrading trend. 4. Complete and sign the re-certification documentation, including the electrician's qualification reference. 5. File the re-certification record in Polaris and confirm the unit's next re-certification due date is correctly scheduled. 6. If any test fails, mark the unit unavailable in Polaris and do not issue re-certification until the fault is corrected and retested.
properties.validation: Confirm all German-standard electrical test results pass and are within the applicable thresholds. Confirm the re-certification documentation is complete, signed by a suitably qualified electrician, and filed in Polaris with the correct next-due date.
properties.procTroubleshooting: If a test result is marginal (close to but within threshold), document the trend and consider a shortened re-certification interval rather than a full pass with no follow-up, particularly for units approaching end of the standard re-certification cycle. If a test fails outright, do not re-test repeatedly hoping for a different result — investigate root cause before retesting.
properties.escalation: Escalate any failed re-certification to NMG Field Engineering and the site's account manager, since the unit must remain out of service until corrected and successfully retested under German regulation.
properties.tags: electrical safety, re-certification, Germany, VDE, Elektrofachkraft, annual
